name: Claude Haiku 4.5 Chat
description: Single-call / multi-turn chat completion with Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5. Available via two gateways: BlockRun (native Anthropic Messages API, default) and yeetful (MCP JSON-RPC tools/call). Pay-per-call in USDC on Base, no API key.

Optional: system, temperature, top_p, top_k, stop_sequences, stream, tools, tool_choice. Returns standard Anthropic message object. ALTERNATE (yeetful): POST https://anthropic.yeetful.com/api/mcp/mcp with header 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' and JSON-RPC 2.0 body {jsonrpc:'2.0',id:1,method:'tools/call',params:{name:'ask_claude',arguments:{prompt,system?}}} (or name:'claude_chat' with arguments:{messages:[{role,content}],system?}). Response is SSE-framed.

messages.content: Reply with the single word: France

usage.outputShape: BlockRun: content[0].text (assistant reply), model, id, type, role, stop_reason, usage.input_tokens, usage.output_tokens. yeetful: SSE 'data:' frame -> JSON-RPC result containing the assistant text.
quirks: MULTI-GATEWAY same op: BlockRun (default) and yeetful are two gateways to Claude Haiku 4.5 with DIFFERENT call shapes — pick by client capability.
BlockRun model field MUST use the slash alias 'anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5' (not the Anthropic dated id). Response echoes the dated id 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'.
BlockRun is the native Anthropic Messages API: model, messages, max_tokens are all REQUIRED. You control max_tokens and model (also routes sonnet/opus aliases on the same endpoint).
BlockRun pricing is dynamic per-token (~$0.0001-$5.00 range); a tiny call costs ~$0.001 — 10x cheaper than yeetful's flat $0.01.

yeetful is an MCP Streamable-HTTP endpoint: body MUST be JSON-RPC 2.0 tools/call (NOT a plain chat payload). Two tools: ask_claude {prompt,system?} single-prompt, claude_chat {messages,system?} multi-turn.
yeetful MUST send header 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' or it returns 406 AFTER charging the $0.01 (charge-then-406 trap on first attempt).
yeetful response is SSE-framed (text/event-stream): strip the 'data: ' prefix and JSON-parse to get the result.
yeetful caps output at 256 tokens and model/max_tokens are server-controlled (cannot override) — use BlockRun if you need longer or controllable output.
yeetful previously reported confirmed:false/txHash:null while still returning 200 with valid content (settlement-reporting quirk).

model.description: The name of the model that will complete your prompt. Choose from our available Sonar models: sonar (lightweight search), sonar-pro (advanced search), sonar-deep-research (exhaustive research), or sonar-reasoning-pro (premier reasoning).

messages.description: A list of messages comprising the conversation so far.

search_mode.description: Controls search mode: 'academic' prioritizes scholarly sources, 'sec' prioritizes SEC filings, 'web' uses general web search. See academic guide and SEC guide.

reasoning_effort.description: Perplexity-Specific: Controls how much computational effort the AI dedicates to each query for deep research models. 'low' provides faster, simpler answers with reduced token usage, 'medium' offers a balanced approach, and 'high' delivers deeper, more thorough responses with increased token usage. This parameter directly impacts the amount of reasoning tokens consumed. WARNING: This parameter is ONLY applicable for sonar-deep-research. Defaults to 'medium' when used with sonar-deep-research.

max_tokens.description: OpenAI Compatible: The maximum number of completion tokens returned by the API. Controls the length of the model's response. If the response would exceed this limit, it will be truncated. Higher values allow for longer responses but may increase processing time and costs.

temperature.description: The amount of randomness in the response, valued between 0 and 2. Lower values (e.g., 0.1) make the output more focused, deterministic, and less creative. Higher values (e.g., 1.5) make the output more random and creative. Use lower values for factual/information retrieval tasks and higher values for creative applications.

top_p.description: OpenAI Compatible: The nucleus sampling threshold, valued between 0 and 1. Controls the diversity of generated text by considering only the tokens whose cumulative probability exceeds the top_p value. Lower values (e.g., 0.5) make the output more focused and deterministic, while higher values (e.g., 0.95) allow for more diverse outputs. Often used as an alternative to temperature.

language_preference.description: Perplexity-Specific: Specifies the preferred language for the chat completion response (i.e., English, Korean, Spanish, etc.) of the response content. This parameter is supported only by the sonar and sonar-pro models. Using it with other models is on a best-effort basis and may not produce consistent results.

search_domain_filter.description: A list of domains to limit search results to. Currently limited to 20 domains for Allowlisting and Denylisting. For Denylisting, add a - at the beginning of the domain string. More information about this here.

return_images.description: Perplexity-Specific: Determines whether search results should include images.

return_related_questions.description: Perplexity-Specific: Determines whether related questions should be returned.

search_recency_filter.description: Perplexity-Specific: Filters search results based on time (e.g., 'week', 'day').

search_after_date_filter.description: Perplexity-Specific: Filters search results to only include content published after this date. Format should be %m/%d/%Y (e.g. 3/1/2025)

search_before_date_filter.description: Perplexity-Specific: Filters search results to only include content published before this date. Format should be %m/%d/%Y (e.g. 3/1/2025)

last_updated_after_filter.description: Perplexity-Specific: Filters search results to only include content last updated after this date. Format should be %m/%d/%Y (e.g. 3/1/2025)

last_updated_before_filter.description: Perplexity-Specific: Filters search results to only include content last updated before this date. Format should be %m/%d/%Y (e.g. 3/1/2025)

top_k.description: OpenAI Compatible: The number of tokens to keep for top-k filtering. Limits the model to consider only the k most likely next tokens at each step. Lower values (e.g., 20) make the output more focused and deterministic, while higher values allow for more diverse outputs. A value of 0 disables this filter. Often used in conjunction with top_p to control output randomness.

stream.description: OpenAI Compatible: Determines whether to stream the response incrementally.

presence_penalty.description: OpenAI Compatible: Positive values increase the likelihood of discussing new topics. Applies a penalty to tokens that have already appeared in the text, encouraging the model to talk about new concepts. Values typically range from 0 (no penalty) to 2.0 (strong penalty). Higher values reduce repetition but may lead to more off-topic text.

frequency_penalty.description: OpenAI Compatible: Decreases likelihood of repetition based on prior frequency. Applies a penalty to tokens based on how frequently they've appeared in the text so far. Values typically range from 0 (no penalty) to 2.0 (strong penalty). Higher values (e.g., 1.5) reduce repetition of the same words and phrases. Useful for preventing the model from getting stuck in loops.

disable_search.description: Perplexity-Specific: When set to true, disables web search completely and the model will only use its training data to respond. This is useful when you want deterministic responses without external information. More information about this here.

enable_search_classifier.description: Perplexity-Specific: Enables a classifier that decides if web search is needed based on your query. See more here.

web_search_options.description: Perplexity-Specific: Configuration for using web search in model responses.

media_response.description: Perplexity-Specific: Configuration for controlling media content in responses, such as videos and images. Use the overrides property to enable specific media types.

name: Baseten Model APIs
description: OpenAI-compatible inference router for hosted open models — DeepSeek V3/V3.1, GLM-4.6/4.7, Kimi K2 variants and gpt-oss-120b — with streaming, tools, structured outputs and controllable reasoning depth.

messages.description: Array of message objects, each with a 'role' (system, user, assistant, tool) and 'content' (string or array of content parts). This is the conversation history sent to the model.

model.description: Model slug to run inference against. Available models: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-0324 (164k context, reasoning), deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1 (164k context, reasoning), zai-org/GLM-4.6 (200k context, reasoning), zai-org/GLM-4.7 (200k context, reasoning), moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Instruct-0905 (128k context), moonshotai/Kimi-K2-Thinking (262k context, always-on reasoning), moonshotai/Kimi-K2.5 (262k context), openai/gpt-oss-120b (128k context). Reasoning models support the reasoning_effort parameter for controlling thinking depth.

frequency_penalty.description: Penalize tokens based on how often they've appeared so far. Range -2.0 to 2.0. Positive values reduce repetition. Default: 0.

logit_bias.description: Map of token IDs to bias values (-100 to 100). Increase or decrease the likelihood of specific tokens appearing in the output.

logprobs.description: If true, returns the log probabilities of each output token in the response.

top_logprobs.description: How many of the most likely tokens (0-20) to return log probabilities for at each position. Requires logprobs to be true.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate in the response. Default is 4096.

n.description: Number of completions to generate. Currently only supports 1.

presence_penalty.description: Penalize tokens based on whether they've appeared at all. Range -2.0 to 2.0. Positive values encourage the model to explore new topics. Default: 0.

response_format.description: Constrain the output format. Use {"type": "json_object"} for JSON mode, or {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": "...", "schema": {...}}} for structured outputs with a specific schema.

seed.description: Integer for deterministic sampling. Same seed with same parameters should return the same result. Not guaranteed across model versions.

stop.description: Up to 4 sequences where the model will stop generating. Can be a string or array of strings.

stream.description: If true, returns server-sent events (SSE) with partial message deltas as tokens are generated, instead of waiting for the full response.

stream_options.description: Options for streaming. Use {"include_usage": true} to get a final chunk with token usage statistics.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature between 0 and 4. Lower values (e.g. 0.2) produce more focused, deterministic output. Higher values (e.g. 1.5) increase creativity. Default is 1.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling threshold between 0 and 1. Only tokens within this cumulative probability mass are considered. 0.1 means only the top 10%. Use as an alternative to temperature.

tools.description: Array of tool/function definitions the model can call. Each tool has {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "...", "description": "...", "parameters": {...}}}. The model may respond with tool_calls instead of content.

tool_choice.description: Controls tool calling behavior. 'auto' lets the model decide, 'none' disables tools, 'required' forces a tool call, or pass {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}} to force a specific tool.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model can make multiple tool calls in parallel in a single response. Default: true.

user.description: A unique string identifying the end user. Useful for abuse monitoring and rate limiting.

top_k.description: Top-K sampling. Only the K most likely next tokens are considered. Lower values make output more focused.

top_p_min.description: Minimum dynamic nucleus sampling threshold. Sets a floor for top_p when using adaptive sampling.

min_p.description: Minimum probability threshold. Tokens below this probability relative to the most likely token are filtered out.

repetition_penalty.description: Multiplicative penalty for repeated tokens. Values > 1.0 discourage repetition, < 1.0 encourage it.

length_penalty.description: Penalty applied during beam search. Values > 1.0 favor longer sequences, < 1.0 favor shorter ones.

early_stopping.description: In beam search, stop as soon as the required number of complete candidates are found.

bad.description: Words or phrases the model should avoid generating. Passed as a string.

bad_token_ids.description: Array of token IDs that should never appear in the output.

stop_token_ids.description: Array of token IDs that will cause generation to stop when produced.

include_stop_str_in_output.description: If true, includes the stop string in the generated output rather than trimming it.

ignore_eos.description: If true, the model continues generating past the end-of-sequence token.

min_tokens.description: Minimum number of tokens to generate before any stop condition can trigger.

skip_special_tokens.description: If true, special tokens are removed from the output text. Default: true.

spaces_between_special_tokens.description: If true, adds spaces between special tokens in the detokenized output.

truncate_prompt_tokens.description: Truncate the prompt to this many tokens if it exceeds the limit, keeping the most recent tokens.

echo.description: If true, prepends the last input message to the generated output.

add_generation_prompt.description: If true, applies the model's generation prompt template. Usually needed for chat models.

add_special_tokens.description: If true, adds special tokens (like BOS) to the input. Default: true.

documents.description: Array of document objects for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Each document has content the model can reference when responding.

chat_template.description: Custom Jinja2 template for formatting the conversation. Overrides the model's default chat template.

chat_template_args.description: Additional arguments passed to the chat template as template variables.

best_of.description: Number of candidate completions to generate server-side, returning the best. Currently only supports 1.

disaggregated_params.description: Advanced parameters for distributed inference. Only relevant for disaggregated serving configurations.

reasoning_effort.description: Controls thinking depth for reasoning models. Options: 'low', 'medium', 'high'. Default: 'medium'. Higher effort uses more tokens but produces more thorough reasoning. Supported on DeepSeek V3/V3.1, GLM 4.6/4.7, and Kimi K2 Thinking.

models.description: Custom council of 2-8 gateway model ids, e.g. ["openai/gpt-5","anthropic/claude-opus","google/gemini-3-pro"] (overrides `mode`). Full selectable list + live prices: GET /api/ai/council/menu.

maxTokens.description: Max output tokens per model. Default 640.

agreement.description: Summary of where the models agreed.

chairman.description: Model id that merged the responses.

usage.callShape: POST https://2s.io/api/ai/council with JSON body { prompt, mode?, models?, maxTokens? } — pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). Result is returned inline in the 200; no polling.

inputExample.prompt: Is a hot dog a sandwich? Give a one-line ruling.

usage.outputShape: data.ok=true; data.items[0] = { consensus (chairman's synthesized answer), confidence (0-1), agreement (where they agreed), dissent[] (points of disagreement), models[]{model,answered,answer} (each member's answer) }; data.total=1; data.source={provider:'2s.io AI Council', url, license:'Generated content — no upstream data license'}; data.meta={mode,chairman,modelCount,answered}; plus top-level meta.cost.usd and meta.settlement{txHash,network,success}.
quirks: Result is nested under data.items[] (an array with one element even for a single question) — read data.items[0].consensus for the merged answer.

DYNAMIC PRICING: the bare/no-body probe quotes ~$0.012, but the real POST body re-quotes higher — mode=fast with a short prompt quoted and settled at $0.0901. Price scales with council size (fast<balanced<deep), maxTokens, and answer length, and is always quoted up front in the 402. Re-read the 402 amount for your exact body before paying.

Billing is 'actual-usage-upto-max': the quoted amount is the max. The exact-scheme accept (first in accepts) charges the full amount; an upto-capable Base client (Permit2) can settle for actual usage (floor $0.001). Observed exact-scheme charge was the full $0.0901.

mode is one of fast (3 quick models) | balanced (3 strong models + peer-refine, default) | deep (5 models + refine). Supplying models[] (2-8 gateway model ids) overrides mode; list live models + prices via GET /api/ai/council/menu.

Models auto-resolve to their latest available version; any unavailable model simply drops out, and at least 2 must answer. Observed run polled claude-haiku-4.5, gemini-3.6-flash, deepseek-v4-flash and merged with chairman anthropic/claude-opus-5.

Free verification without paying: append ?trial=1 (or header X-2s-Trial:1) for one free real call per endpoint per hour — the hourly trial for this endpoint was already consumed during indexing, so validation was done via the paid call.
prompt max length 12000 chars; maxTokens 128-4096 (default 640).
usage.guide: Ask a panel of frontier models one question and get a single merged answer. POST https://2s.io/api/ai/council with JSON body {"prompt":"<your question>"}; optionally set "mode" to fast|balanced|deep (default balanced), or "models":[...] (2-8 gateway ids from GET /api/ai/council/menu) to override the preset, and "maxTokens" (128-4096, default 640). Pay per call via x402 (USDC on Base or Solana). Price is DYNAMIC and quoted in the 402 — it scales with council size and answer length (mode=fast short prompt = ~$0.09; re-read the 402 amount for your body before paying). Read the merged answer from data.items[0].consensus, with data.items[0].confidence, data.items[0].dissent[], and each member's answer in data.items[0].models[]. Result is synchronous in the 200; no polling. Verified 2026-07-30 with {prompt:'Is a hot dog a sandwich? Give a one-line ruling.', mode:'fast'} → HTTP 200, $0.0901 charged (tx 0xa34beee8...).
